content_units: Auckland Remote-Work Internet Fit

For a 2-person Auckland household with frequent video calls, occasional 4K streaming, a budget under   NZD 95/month  , and a preference for   no long contract  ,   Plan 2 and Plan 1   are the real contenders. The fastest plan is impressive, but it is not the best value for your stated needs.
Plan-by-Plan Comparison
Plan   Speed   Monthly Cost   Contract   Modem   Effective Monthly Cost   Fit for Your Needs
Plan 1   300/100 Mbps   NZD 79   12 months   Included     NZD 79     Strong performance; best speed/value trade-off
Plan 2   100/20 Mbps   NZD 65   Month-to-month   NZD 10/month     NZD 75     Best flexibility; enough for remote work and 4K
Plan 3   900/500 Mbps   NZD 99   Month-to-month   Bring your own     NZD 99+     Over budget; likely overkill unless heavy uploads matter
Best Fit for Your Priorities
Recommended pick:   Plan 2
-   Best match for your budget and flexibility goals
- Total monthly cost is about   NZD 75   with the modem fee, still comfortably under budget
-   100/20 Mbps   is typically enough for:
- multiple HD video calls
- one 4K stream
- normal cloud work, browsing, and file syncing
- Month-to-month terms reduce commitment risk if service quality disappoints or your needs change
Why it wins:   Your requirement says “no long contract if possible,” and Plan 2 satisfies that while still meeting a remote worker household’s likely usage.
Runner-up:   Plan 1
- Better performance headroom than Plan 2
-   300/100 Mbps   is excellent for video calls, streaming, large downloads, and stronger multi-device comfort
- Included modem keeps pricing simple
- Main downside:   12-month contract
When Plan 1 is better:   Choose it if you expect frequent large uploads, regular simultaneous heavy usage, or want extra stability margin and are comfortable locking in for a year.
Is the Fastest Plan Worth It?
Short answer:   No, not for this use case
Plan 3’s   900/500 Mbps   is far beyond what most 2-person remote-work homes need for stable video calls and occasional 4K streaming.
What that extra speed actually buys you:
- faster large downloads
- much faster cloud backups/uploads
- more capacity for many heavy users at once
- smoother performance during very high simultaneous usage
Why it is probably not worth it here:
- It is   over your NZD 95 budget
- You may also need to buy a modem/router, increasing real cost further
- Video calls usually depend more on   latency, Wi‑Fi quality, and network stability   than extreme headline speed
- Occasional 4K streaming does not need anywhere near 900 Mbps
A practical view:
- Good video calling often works well on far less than 100 Mbps
- 4K streaming usually needs only a fraction of Plan 2’s total bandwidth
- The jump from 300 Mbps to 900 Mbps is noticeable mainly for power users, heavy uploaders, or large households
Decision Guide for Your Situation
- Pick   Plan 2   if you want the   best overall fit  : lower commitment, under budget, adequate performance
- Pick   Plan 1   if you are happy with a contract and want   more speed cushion   for not much more money
- Skip   Plan 3   unless your household does frequent big file uploads, heavy NAS/cloud backup, or you simply want premium performance regardless of value
